title: Consolidate Console HTTP/GraphQL handlers and cache strategy to cut p95 latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
The console backend has accumulated multiple divergent HTTP and GraphQL handler implementations that perform overlapping data fetches and inconsistent caching. This ticket consolidates those handlers, introduces a unified read-through caching layer, and rewrites the response stitching path to reduce duplicated DB/metalayer calls. Goal: reduce console p95 latency by at least 35% for common dashboard routes and reduce request CPU by 20%.

Background / Why now:
- Recent SLO breaches on console dashboard p95 during larger tenant workloads (Datadog: https://datadog.example/redwood/console-latency).
- Profiling shows duplicated fetches from multiple resolvers and middleware (see flamegraphs: https://perf.redwood/console-2026-03).
- Several hotfixes and small refactors left inconsistent caching TTLs and eviction logic.
- Upgrades to graphql-js and our HTTP middleware were deferred; memory and serialization hotspots observed.

Proposal:
1) Consolidate overlapping REST handlers and GraphQL resolvers behind a small set of canonical 'data fetch' modules. These modules will: perform batched DB calls, use a shared DataLoader, and expose stable typed responses.
2) Implement a read-through cache abstraction with pluggable backends (in-memory LRU for single-node development, Redis for prod). Cache keys and TTLs will be standardized and documented.
3) Replace ad-hoc response-merging code with a streaming merger that avoids materializing full large response objects when clients only need a subset (esp. large route list responses).
4) Upgrade graphql-js to 17.x and express middleware to the latest stable, addressing known memory leaks and enabling better instrumentation.
5) Add feature flag for progressive rollout (feature: console.handler_consolidation).

Acceptance criteria (must pass for close):
- End-to-end p95 for /dashboard and /routes endpoints reduced by >=35% in staging load tests.
- CPU usage per request reduced by >=20% on representative trace loads.
- No increase in error rate (5xx) in canary (≤ 0.1% delta).
- Automated integration tests for cache correctness (stale reads, invalidation scenarios) added.
- Migration docs and runbook for rollback present in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/console-handler-consolidation.

Implementation tasks:
- [ ] Profile and capture baseline (flamegraphs + Datadog dashboards). Owner: Rajat. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3781 - WIP)
- [ ] Extract canonical fetch modules and replace duplicated calls across resolver layers. Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Implement DataLoader wrapping for batched DB access (unit tests required). Owner: Miguel.
- [ ] Implement pluggable read-through cache abstraction with Redis adapter and in-memory fallback. Owner: Rajat.
- [ ] Standardize cache key formats and TTL policy (documented). Owner: Ava.
- [ ] Rewrite response merger to stream deltas to client where supported (fallback to legacy full objects behind feature flag). Owner: Priya.
- [ ] Upgrade graphql-js and express; run compatibility tests and patch interfaces. Owner: Miguel.
- [ ] Add end-to-end load test harness and run staged canary deployment. Owner: SRE (contact: Lian Zhou).
- [ ] Observability: add tracing spans, metrics (per-resolver latency, cache hit/miss rates), and dashboard. Owner: Rajat.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): extract canonical modules + local tests. Feature flag off.
- Phase 1 (staging canary): enable consolidated handlers for 10% of traffic in staging; run load-tests.
- Phase 2 (internal canary): enable feature flag for internal team environment; collect metrics 48h.
- Phase 3 (production gradual): enable for 5% production traffic, monitor for 72h; increase to 25% then 100% if safe.
- Rollback: flip feature flag off; rollback PRs if progressive rollout reveals regression. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/console-handler-consolidation#runbook.

Monitoring & KPIs:
- Datadog dashboard: console.handler_consolidation (p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/req, cache hit ratio).
- Alert if p95 increases >10% of baseline or error rate increases >0.05%.
- SLO target: console UI p95 < 400ms for primary routes under standard tenant load.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: cache invalidation bugs cause stale admin data. Mitigation: conservative TTLs + write-through invalidation hooks on writes; end-to-end tests.
- Risk: upgrade to graphql-js introduces API surface changes. Mitigation: compatibility wrapper + integration test suite.
- Risk: Redis outage affects reads. Mitigation: in-memory fallback and circuit-breaker to degrade gracefully.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/console-handler-consolidation
- PR (initial extraction): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/3781
- Load test repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtests/tree/console-2026

Notes / Progress updates:
- 2026-03-02: Baseline profiling completed (Datadog + local flamegraphs). Found 3 resolvers making identical tenant metadata calls.
- 2026-03-04: Spike: extracted tenant fetch module and replaced two resolvers in a feature branch. Local p95 dropped ~22% for small synthetic traces. PR opened: #3781.
- 2026-03-06: Implemented DataLoader prototype; observed 30% fewer DB connections in dev. Running unit tests.
- 2026-03-09: Started cache abstraction; landed in-memory LRU adapter for dev. Redis adapter skeleton in review.
- 2026-03-11: Compatibility tests failing for a subsection of GraphQL directives after upgrade; Miguel working on shim.
- 2026-03-12: SRE confirms readiness for staging canary once Redis adapter lands and integration tests pass.

Review notes (from PM & Design):
- PM (Jules): prioritize correct cache invalidation over aggressive TTLs to avoid stale console state for workspace admins.
- Design (Maya): streaming deltas should preserve backward-compatible response shape; add a response-version header for clients to opt in.

Next steps (short term):
- Finish Redis adapter and wire circuit-breaker (Rajat).
- Fix graphql-js shim issues (Miguel).
- Add integration tests for cache invalidation scenarios (Priya).
- Schedule staging canary for 2026-03-20 pending test results.
